legend.name: Hen
legend.meaning: Red-brown, like a Rhode Island Red

note.text: Stage 1. A hen lays an egg with a hard shell. If it was fertilized, an embryo can grow inside when it's kept warm.
note.remember: Bird eggs have hard shells; frog eggs have jelly.

note.text: Stage 2. The hen sits on the egg to keep it at about 37.5 °C. Inside, the embryo grows for 21 days.

steps.title: Growing chick
steps.instruction: Draw the curled-up embryo inside the egg.

note.text: The embryo feeds on the yolk. Near the end, it fills the whole egg and gets ready to hatch.

steps.title: Chick
steps.instruction: Trace the chick's body and head.

note.text: Stage 3. The chick pecks its way out of the shell using a tiny bump on its beak called the egg tooth.
note.remember: Chicks are covered in soft down, not feathers.

steps.title: Beak, eye and feet
steps.instruction: Draw the chick's beak, eye and feet.

note.text: Chicks can walk and peck for food within hours of hatching.

steps.title: Hen
steps.instruction: Trace the adult hen's body and head.

note.text: Stage 4. In about 5 months the chick grows into an adult. A hen can then lay eggs, starting the cycle again.

steps.title: Beak and legs
steps.instruction: Draw the hen's beak, eye and legs.

note.text: Strong legs and feet let chickens scratch the ground to find seeds and insects.

steps.title: Comb
steps.instruction: Trace the comb on the hen's head.

note.text: The comb is red skin on top of the head, full of blood vessels. It helps the chicken lose heat on hot days.
note.remember: Chickens can't sweat; the comb helps them cool down.

steps.title: The cycle
steps.instruction: Draw the arrows from stage to stage, going clockwise.

note.text: The adult hen lays eggs, and the cycle starts again. Unlike a butterfly or frog, a chick already looks like a small adult.

steps.title: Color
steps.instruction: These are a chicken's real colors, simplified.

steps.title: Stage order
steps.instruction: Tap the stages in order, starting from the egg.
steps.why: A fertilized egg develops into an embryo, which hatches as a chick and grows into an adult.
steps.hint: What grows inside the egg before it hatches?

steps.title: Label the stages
steps.instruction: Pick the right name for each numbered stage.

targets.role: Laid by the hen, with a hard protective shell.
Grows inside the egg for 21 days, feeding on the yolk.

mistakes.Chick: This one hasn't hatched yet. Inside the egg, it's an embryo.

targets.role: Hatched, covered in down, and able to walk.
A grown female chicken that lays eggs.

commonMistakes.Tadpole: Tadpoles are young frogs. Chickens hatch already looking like small birds.
commonMistakes.Larva: Larvae are found in insects and frogs. A chick isn't one.

steps.title: Explain
steps.question: How is a chicken's life cycle different from a butterfly's?

options.text: A chick already looks like a small adult; a caterpillar looks nothing like a butterfly
options.feedback: Yes. Chickens just grow bigger. Butterflies go through metamorphosis, changing their whole body.
They do: every chick hatches from an egg.
Both have four stages, but a butterfly's change shape completely.
Chicks live on land from the moment they hatch.
